sections.brief: Sophia's 'Evangelical Gnostics' label defined once; 'Gnosticism' coined by Henry More, category debate (Williams, King, Brakke); Simon Magus as a founder built by Irenaeus; Basilides (365 heavens, Simon of Cyrene); Carpocratians ('style themselves Gnostics', Marcellina in Rome); Valentinus (Tertullian's bishopric story, city unnamed), Ptolemy, Heracleon, Theodotus, Letter to Flora; Sethians as a modern category; Marcionites, Manichaeans, Cathars kept apart; Mandaeans today (60-100k, Iraq after 2003); Doinel's Église Gnostique 1890. Figures: compare (groups and sources)

Salvation by knowing (Thomas 1, 70; Irenaeus I.21); Apocryphon of John myth (Barbelo, Sophia, Yaltabaoth's 'jealous God', five seals) with antisemitism guardrail; Valentinian demiurge as 'just' (Flora), three classes of people; present resurrection (Philip, Treatise on the Resurrection); Ptolemy's three-part Law; answers to Ron: kingdom within yes (Thomas 3, 113, Mary; Luke 17:21 read 'within' by Fathers per Ramelli), ascent yes (Mary, Irenaeus I.21, Origen's Ophite diagram, Zostrianos/Allogenes), alchemy not in their texts (Zosimos bridge, Fraser 2007); labelled interpretation passage (Jung, spiritual alchemy). Figures: flow (Apocryphon of John fall and return); compare (The teaching questions)

Rites (Philip's five mysteries, five seals, Irenaeus I.21 redemption rites); women (Marcellina, Marcus's women prophets, Tertullian Prescr. 41; Thomas 114 caveat); loose offices and Valentinians inside churches (AH III.15.2); answers to Ron: tithe none documented (Apocryphon of John curse on selling the teaching; Irenaeus's hostile Marcus allegation; proto-orthodox voluntary giving, Justin 67; first tithe canons 567/585), commandments (Mary 'no law as the lawgiver'; Thomas 6, 14; Ptolemy keeps the Decalogue), Sunday/feast duty none documented (Thomas 27, Ptolemy; assemblies per Constantine's edict; 321 law later). Figures: compare (practice questions, Gnostic vs proto-orthodox)

Irenaeus c.180 (succession list, Rome's preeminent authority); Tertullian's praescriptio; Refutation of All Heresies (Athos 1842); Origen c.248; Plotinus Ennead II.9; Epiphanius Panarion 374-377; Constantine's edict (Valentinians named, assemblies banned, houses confiscated, books searched for); CTh 16.1.2 (380) and 16.5; Athanasius 367 no destruction order; what the record does not show (no executions, no named Gnostic-book burning order); Pagels 1979 thesis and critics (Chadwick, Maccoby, Brown). Figures: time (c.180-380)
